style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Macro photograph of an unbranded high bandwidth memory stack with eight visible DRAM layers on a base die, set beside a taller twelve-layer stack on an anti-static mat inside a data hall. A single soft key light from the left rakes low across the chips, carving deep shadows and revealing matte black packaging, thin gold interconnect edges, and faint dust. Split-screen diptych: left half short stack, right half tall stack; 100mm macro lens, razor-thin focal plane on top layers, background server racks falling into dark bokeh. Graphite, slate grey, one amber highlight, fine film grain.
rationale: The story turns on the physical architecture difference between 8-Hi and 12-Hi HBM stacks and its per-gigabit cost consequence. A 100mm macro lens makes the layer count and base die tangible, while a split-screen diptych contrasts the two heights directly. The data hall setting grounds the memory stack in the real infrastructure environment.
cue: the shorter stack costs more per bit
subject: high bandwidth memory stack with eight DRAM layers on a base die beside a taller twelve-layer stack
core_thesis: Samsung's 2027 HBM supply is already sold at agreed prices, with the shorter 8-Hi stack costing 10–20% more per gigabit than 12-Hi because both stacks share one base die, so the only remaining budget lever is to need less memory.
core_conflict: per-gigabit cost penalty of the shorter 8-Hi stack versus the fixed base-die overhead shared with 12-Hi, forcing buyers to reduce memory demand rather than negotiate price
composition: split-screen diptych; left half short stack, right half tall stack
alt_text: High bandwidth memory stack with eight layers next to a taller twelve-layer stack, showing per-bit cost difference.
caption: A shorter 8-Hi memory stack sits beside a taller 12-Hi stack, making the higher per-gigabit cost physically visible.
title: 8-Hi vs 12-Hi HBM stack cost comparison

review.depicts: Two stacks of dark square plates with gold-toned edges, a shorter one on the left and a taller one on the right, each on a metallic base on a textured grey surface.
review.reason: The split diptych directly illustrates the article's comparison between a shorter 8-Hi HBM stack and a taller 12-Hi stack.
